thread.title: Missoula County seeks public input for Family Justice Center planning process
thread.title_full: Missoula County seeks public input for Family Justice Center planning process

author: G. J. Dupree
title: Missoula County seeks public input for Family Justice Center planning process
text:
Missoula County invites the public to join a strategic planning session for a possible Family Justice Center, which would provide resources and support for crime survivors and their families in one location, according to a March 24 announcement.
The planning session is scheduled for Wednesday and Thursday, April 1-2, at the Broadway Building Conference Center at St. Patrick Hospital. The event will run from 8:30 a.m. to 3:45 p.m. on Wednesday and from 8 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. on Thursday. Registration is required, and interested residents can email organizers to participate. Media representatives are also welcome at any part of the session.
A Family Justice Center brings together agencies such as law enforcement, prosecutors, advocates, therapists, civil attorneys and community organizations in one coordinated approach to support those affected by domestic violence, sexual assault, child abuse or related trauma.
Staff from the Family Justice Center Alliance will facilitate the sessions onsite. The Community Justice Department encourages all stakeholders—and especially individuals who have experienced domestic violence—to participate or provide feedback about the project.
“A Family Justice Center makes a real difference, not just for survivors, but for the teams working to support them,” said Celedina Coss, licensed clinical social worker and division manager for Missoula County’s Crime Victim Advocate division. “When someone can walk into one place and access everything they need, it reduces confusion, removes barriers and meets them where they’re at during a really difficult time. On our side, bringing partners together in one space with a shared purpose allows us to respond more effectively and collaboratively, which ultimately leads to better outcomes for survivors and the community.”
The county received $700,000 in grant funding that supports this planning phase. Officials say they aim to fund any future facility through grants or fundraising rather than local property taxes.
The first Family Justice Center was created in San Diego in 2002 through collaboration between city attorneys’ offices and police departments alongside community-based agencies addressing domestic violence issues. Montana currently has one such center—the Northern Lights Family Justice Center located in Billings.
This project is supported by Grant No. 15JOVW-24-GG-01632-ICJR awarded by the Office on Violence Against Women of the U.S. Department of Justice.
